title: Dynamical one-from-many quantum metrology: Sum rule and matrix-free precision bound
abstract: Practical quantum single-parameter estimation is rarely a pristine task; it almost invariably involves nuisance parameters, casting it as a one-from-many problem. Existing approaches to this problem rely on multi-parameter metrology, reducing the matrix quantum Cramér-Rao bound to obtain scalar quantum precision limits. However, these methods are often hampered by the demanding inversion of the quantum Fisher information (QFI) matrix and the requisite choice of a weight matrix, and they break down when the QFI matrix becomes singular. Here, we show that for dynamical one-from-many estimation, a previously overlooked sum rule connecting the QFI about all model parameters to the QFI about time necessitates including the latter to consider an augmented QFI matrix while simultaneously rendering it inherently singular--precisely the scenario where conventional approaches fail. To meet this challenge, we derive a tight, matrix-free quantum precision bound that involves only scalar quantities, offers broad applicability, and subsumes existing results as special cases. Validated in both unitary and noisy settings, our findings provide a refined operational framework for practical quantum single-parameter metrology.
summary: This paper develops a novel, matrix-free quantum precision bound for estimating parameters in complex quantum systems where multiple nuisance parameters are present. It overcomes the limitations of traditional methods that fail when the Quantum Fisher Information matrix is singular. The resulting bound offers a robust and general framework for achieving optimal measurement strategies in open quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of quantum single-parameter estimation when multiple nuisance parameters are present, known as the 'one-from-many' problem.
main_result: A tight, matrix-free quantum precision bound is derived that avoids the need to invert the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) matrix, offering a general framework for practical metrology.
method: The authors derive the bound by combining the generalized uncertainty relation with error propagation formulas, leading to a maximum over scalar bounds associated with each parameter.
model_or_system: The analysis is applied to dynamical quantum processes governed by the Lindblad master equation, modeling systems like two-qubit interactions or quantum thermometry.
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) matrix elements, expectation values of observables ($\langle O angle$), and response functions ($\Delta_x\langle Oangle$).
important_parameters: Time ($t$), coupling strengths ($\omega, \lambda, \Gamma$), and dissipation rates ($\gamma$).
main_assumptions: The framework assumes the applicability of the general bound derived from combining uncertainty relations and error propagation, which is designed to handle singular QFI matrices.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate comparisons between the proposed bound, the standard QCRB, and the actual variance for various physical models (unitary, thermometry, two-qubit), showing where the proposed bound is tighter.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem in multi-parameter metrology, derives a sum rule connecting QFI elements, and then introduces the general matrix-free bound. It validates this bound across multiple physical examples (unitary, thermometry, two-qubit) using specific observables and parameter sets.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, general tool for quantifying measurement precision in open quantum systems, directly applicable to characterizing decoherence rates or interaction strengths in complex quantum devices.
